paper.title: Measuring higher education: comparing Danish survey and register data in the study of values
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability: 'The data for this study is available from The Danish National Archives: …

registers.name_in_paper: official education registers / the Statistics Denmark education registers
registers.role: treatment and classification: register-based highest educational attainment, ISCED-classified; also the benchmark against which survey self-reports are judged
variables_mentioned: educational attainment (ISCED categories; 'unknown' merged with primary education before data release)

registers.role: controls: annual individual income, categorised into four groups
sample frame and controls: gender and residential region

linkages: When the two random samples were drawn from the Statistics Denmark population database, annual individual income, residential region and educational attainment were linked to individuals using official tax and education registers
Survey respondents in the Danish branch of EVS2017 are linked to their own register records at the individual level; both surveys were conducted by the survey department of Statistics Denmark

sample.universe: The Danish population, sampled as two independent random samples for the Danish branch of the European Values Study 2017 (EVS2017), differing only in the mode of data collection
selection_rules: Two random samples drawn from the Statistics Denmark population database
Only survey respondents are included in the dataset obtained from the Danish National Archives
Tertiary-educated subsample (Table 1): respondents who either reported tertiary education in the survey or were registered as having tertiary education as their highest level (N = 1774)
Under-reporting (2.5% of the tertiary sample) is excluded from the analyses of factors associated with discrepant reporting and from the examination of correlations with values
Table 3 linear probability model estimated on N = 1651
Secondary-track analysis (Fig. 4, Appendix Tables 8-10) restricted to respondents who reported secondary education, thereby excluding the over-reporters
'Don't know' answers on the value items are coded missing
sample.period: September 2017 to January 2018 (CAPI from September 2017; CAWI/PAPI mainly December 2017 and January 2018)
sample.n_observations: 3362 respondents in the full Danish EVS2017 sample (Table 2); 1774 in the tertiary-educated subsample (Table 1); 1651 in the Table 3 regression

construction_notes: Educational information from the questionnaire is classified to correspond to the register-based measure according to the standard ISCED classification (OECD 2022)

Short-cycle tertiary education (ISCED 5) is a single questionnaire category; medium-cycle tertiary (ISCED 6) combines 'university BA' and 'medium-cycle tertiary' (e.g. nurses, teachers, engineers, journalists); long-cycle tertiary combines 'university MA' (ISCED 7) and 'research education'/PhD (ISCED 8)
The register 'unknown' education category was merged with the primary education category prior to data release, so the exact number of register missings cannot be identified
The over-reporting indicator equals 1 when the respondent reported tertiary education but no corresponding qualification was recorded in the registers
Mode of data collection is taken from EVS2017 variable V4, distinguishing CAPI from the self-administered modes (CAWI or PAPI)

Age at immigration is calculated from survey variables V234 (birth year) and V237 (year of immigration to Denmark); reference category is born in Denmark, with immigrants split at age 26, a threshold chosen from OECD (2022) graduation-age statistics
Income categorisation and the overall age groupings are adopted from the main EVS 2017 report (Frederiksen 2019)
All independent variables in Table 3 are categorical and were transformed into dummy variables, with the largest category of each variable serving as the reference category

Six EVS2017 questions were selected as indicators of attitudes towards gender equality, environmental protection, immigration, homosexuality, income equality and state-provided social security (Appendix Table 7)

Three of the six value items are measured on a 1-10 scale (homosexuality, income equality, state-provided social security) and three on a Likert agree-disagree scale (gender equality, immigration, environmental protection)
Analyses run in R version 4.5.1; Table 3 produced with the stargazer package (Hlavac 2022)

claims.statement: Respondents interviewed in person (CAPI) are more likely to report tertiary education that is not recorded in the registers than respondents who answered a self-administered questionnaire.

treatment.label: Interviewer (CAPI)

register_source.value: EVS2017 survey variable V4 (mode of data collection)

definition.value: Dummy = 1 for respondents interviewed face-to-face (Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing), 0 for the self-administered modes (CAWI/PAPI); taken from EVS2017 variable V4. Reference category: CAWI/PAPI.

timing.value: Measured at the time of the EVS2017 interview (2017-2018); income, region and gender taken from the registers at the time the sample was drawn

outcome.label: Over-reporting of tertiary education

register_source.value: Constructed by comparing the EVS2017 self-reported education question with educational attainment from the Statistics Denmark education registers; no DST variable codes are named

definition.value: Binary indicator of whether respondents reported tertiary education when no corresponding qualification was recorded in the registers; respondents who reported a LOWER level than recorded (2.5%) are excluded from the analysis

timing.value: Measured at the time of the EVS2017 interview (September 2017 - January 2018), against the register record linked when the sample was drawn

units.value: change in the probability of reporting tertiary education not recorded in the registers (0-1 dependent variable), relative to the reference category

estimand.target_population: Danish EVS2017 respondents who reported or were registered with tertiary education

population.description: Respondents in the Danish branch of EVS2017 who either reported tertiary education in the survey or were registered with tertiary education as their highest attainment; under-reporters (2.5%) and respondents missing on the survey education question are excluded
subgroups_defined: mode of data collection (CAPI vs CAWI/PAPI)
population.selection: Survey respondents only (CAPI: 1696 of 3380 invited, 50%; CAWI/PAPI: 1666 of 4004, 42%); the data-collection team found respondents had a higher mean age than non-respondents and that medium- and long-cycle tertiary categories were slightly overrepresented among respondents

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in respondent characteristics within two independent random samples of the Danish population (EVS2017); no reform, lottery or discontinuity is used

key_assumptions.assumption: The analysis is associational: the coefficients are differences between each subgroup and its reference category, net of the other categorical variables in the model; no exogenous variation is used and no causal identification argument is made
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper frames the exercise as exploring 'potential causes' and reports 'significant predictors' / factors 'associated with' discrepant reporting

key_assumptions.assumption: The administrative register is treated as the accurate benchmark, so a mismatch in which the survey reports more education is interpreted as over-reporting by the respondent
key_assumptions.supported_by: 'Given the high quality and completeness of Danish registers, the observed divergence is interpreted primarily as over-reporting', while the paper also states that neither source is assumed free from error

key_assumptions.assumption: Linear probability model: the conditional probability of over-reporting is additive and linear in the dummy regressors
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 3 note: 'Linear probability model'; text names the LPM estimator

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on responding to the EVS2017 survey and on being tertiary-educated by either the survey or the register measure
key_assumptions.supported_by: Non-response analysis reported by the data collectors (Toubol and Frederiksen 2019); the tertiary-educated subsample is defined in Section 5.1

threats_discussed: social desirability: respondents affirming a socially valued characteristic in personal interviews
time lag between the registration of educational information and the interview date, during which some students may have completed their education
respondents reporting ongoing rather than completed education (the Danish question wording asks for the 'highest educational level')
non-recognition of foreign qualifications earned abroad
non-response bias: respondents older than non-respondents; medium- and long-cycle tertiary slightly overrepresented
mode of data collection interacts with age, so age must be controlled for
robustness_checks: age measured as a continuous variable, then with a quadratic term
youngest age category split into 18-21 and 22-26 years
self-reported household income deciles instead of register-based personal income
alternative age-at-immigration thresholds of 22, 24 and 28 years
unresolved_confounders: information on ongoing education was not available in the dataset
direct information on foreign qualifications is unavailable; age at immigration is used as a proxy
only educational level, and not educational field or specific subjects, has been examined

estimation.specification: Linear probability model of a binary over-reporting indicator on dummy variables for mode of data collection, gender, age group, register income group, region and age at immigration, each variable's largest category serving as reference; no equation is printed
